reuse.why: The tree already exports getScheduledAmount from shared/schedules.ts (used by SchedulesTable, Balance, mobile schedules); the diff adds a second, near-identically named getScheduleAmount beside it, re-writes the 7.5% tolerance instead of calling getApproxNumberThreshold, and the API's toExternal re-implements the range rule inline.

duplication.why: Two parallel 'expected amount' helpers now coexist, the tolerance formula is duplicated from shared/rules.ts, and api-models.ts carries its own furthest-from-zero copy that already disagrees with the new lowest-value rule.

placement.why: The new helper sits in shared/schedules.ts and the server sites call it, but the API field computes the rule in api-models.ts instead of the shared layer.

scope.why: Edits are confined to the schedule-amount sites, API model/handler types and tests, though several comments are left stale ('endpoint furthest from zero').

maintainability.why: A maintainer must know that getScheduleAmount, getScheduledAmount and the inline API copy all encode the same rule differently, and that each caller still owns the missing-amount dispatch; the next rule change will again miss sites.

bypasses_abstraction.where: New getScheduleAmount bypasses the existing getScheduledAmount (shared/schedules.ts, used by desktop-client); scheduleModel.toExternal in api-models.ts bypasses both; the isapprox tolerance bypasses getApproxNumberThreshold (shared/rules.ts).

disguised_duplication.where: getScheduleAmount is a renamed sibling of the existing getScheduledAmount; the tolerance is getApproxNumberThreshold rewritten inline; the API range rule is a reshaped ternary copy in toExternal.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduleAmount gains an op parameter and an isapprox branch; scheduleModel.toExternal (api-models.ts) re-implements the rule inline and getScheduledAmount with its desktop-client callers stays a separate definition outside the new helper; callers in schedules/app.ts and computeSchedulePreviewTransactions keep their own null ? 0 dispatch.
